### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **20** documentable anchor(s).

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e0cba9ddd7dcd0991ceb47fb4d86ce556961c8bf`.

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e0cba9ddd7dcd0991ceb47fb4d86ce556961c8bf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e6941ff8872063ea7443282907aa0316bba6ce68` — the merge of head `e63ab141c1999ca3da4cd84a30259875d6128081` into base `e0cba9ddd7dcd0991ceb47fb4d86ce556961c8bf`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e6941ff8872063ea7443282907aa0316bba6ce68 && git checkout e6941ff8872063ea7443282907aa0316bba6ce68
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e0cba9ddd7dcd0991ceb47fb4d86ce556961c8bf e63ab141c1999ca3da4cd84a30259875d6128081 && git checkout -B drift-repro e0cba9ddd7dcd0991ceb47fb4d86ce556961c8bf && git merge --no-ff e63ab141c1999ca3da4cd84a30259875d6128081

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e0cba9ddd7dcd0991ceb47fb4d86ce556961c8bf
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e0cba9ddd7dcd0991ceb47fb4d86ce556961c8bf` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e0d92b7b98984731fc0968255ee362c3a19287ba`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.record-currency-follow-pair-refused-on-install-and-reload.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-registration.ts, packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-artifact-refusal-restores.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/record-currency-guards.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-register-refusal.test.ts (narrowing face: the whole diff outside the prose faces). Cited code, read and not reviewed: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/batch-object-registration.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/registry-question.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/customization-package.ts, docs/adr/0029, 0087, 0144, 0146. The `.changeset` file and `content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx` are the lane seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set, install and upgrade through the `manifest` service on a sealed registry: narrowed. Right.** `restoringOnRefusal` ends the outermost run with `recordCurrencyFollowRefusalOfRun`; a refused pair throws `RecordCurrencyFollowRefusedError` (`INVALID_METADATA`, 422) from inside the run, so the existing restore puts the artifact back. Read in `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`: a declared 4xx answers `422 PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED` on both branches before the ledger write.
- **Accept set, artifact reload: narrowed twice. Right, on the tree's precedent.** A bad pair is now refused, and it refuses the whole reload. On `main` each package was its own run and the flat objects registered outside any run; `refreshReloadedPackages` already refuses a reload whole when `refusePicklistArrival(..., { act: 'reload' })` refuses it.
- **Accept set, parent end with the child outside the run: narrowed, and under-declared. Wrong as documented (S1).** The door asked of a parent layer the run registered reads every registered child. A package whose object is only the parent is refused when a tenant's or another package's child follows a field it does not hold as a code, including when this upgrade changed nothing in the pair. The CONTROL pin shows the mechanism; the upgrade-guide entry names only pairs on the package's own objects.
- **Owner layer under a tenant overlay not asked: right.** `resolveObject` serves `overlay ?? own`, and the late-install branch re-classifies in place, which the run's end reads because it holds the contributor itself.
- **Public surface, `SchemaRegistry.restoringOnRefusal`: signature unchanged, nested behaviour changed. Right, and declared.** A nested call puts back its own writes before it throws. The callers in the tree are the `manifest` service, `registerApp` and the batch judge; only the reload catches a nested refusal.
- **Unmoved, confirmed in the tree:** the cold boot (seal set at `kernel:bootstrapped`, after the ledger rehydrate), bare `registerObject`, the batch judge (always throws its sentinel inside its own run, so the run's end is never reached), and a `metadata:reloaded` announce that carries no `metadata`.
- **Nothing is widened.**

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/objectql` minor, `@objectstack/spec` patch: matches. `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` asks that a declared kind grade at least one moved package minor; objectql is that package and spec moves only by the entry.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` are both right: a value an author could install is now refused.
- ADR-0087: the changeset marker names the entry's id, the file name follows the entries README, and no D2 conversion is correct (only the author knows the code field). The BREAKING banner, the Was/Now mapping and the author's fix are in the changeset body.
- The entry's statements on 422, `PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED`, `reload refused`, `hotLoaded` and the cold boot agree with the code read. Its omissions are S1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Reload premise corrected (the reload was not one run).** Answered: the correction is true on `main`, and the whole-reload refusal has the picklist precedent. The ruling "no product fork" and the two surface extensions (`registry.ts`, the spec entry) are on the card only inside the dev session's re-posted claims 6837234363 and 6837447204; the seat's ACCEPT should state them in its own words.
- **Open question (overlay that lacks the code field a new child follows).** Escalated to the maintainer; not decided here. Two readings for that ruling:
  - ADR-0146 D2's advisory clause does not govern this case. It speaks of declared overrides in a paired `.custom` package, and `OVERRIDE_TYPE_CLASSIFICATION` lists `object` as `extend_only` (D10). The as-built refusal contradicts no ruling of record, and nothing obliges the alternative.
  - The remedy the report gives for the as-built reading is not shown reachable (S2).
- **Stale clause in `registry-question.ts` ("which nothing else asks").** Confirmed stale, and already stale for the batch writers since #32474. `carrier: none` leaves it unowned; the seat files the follow-up.
- **`security_findings: none`.** Nothing found here either; no item is with the seat.
- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no note owed.
- **Check-runs:** none failed. Still running when read at 2026-11-12T23:51Z: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Type Check · workspace, Type Check UI. This record does not stand in for them.

### ④ Design judgment

**Hits file (the upgrade-guide entry).** It holds against the code for the cases it names. Two findings:

- **S1, should-fix.** The entry's `surface` and its "packages installed before this release" sentence cover only a pair the package itself holds. The tree also refuses a package that holds only the parent end, because of a child it does not own, and the fix is then with the child's holder, which `replacement` never says. Add the class and its remedy, and one pin for an unchanged parent re-registered over an outside bad child.
- **S2, should-fix, tied to the escalated question.** The entry and the changeset are silent on the overlay refusal the code pins. The report's remedy ("the customer adds the field to the customized object") is unproven: the pin builds the overlay with a direct `registerObject`, and ADR-0029 D9.6 says the save gate refuses an overlay write to a packaged object `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` every time. Once the maintainer rules, state the case and a remedy checked against the write doors, or the alternative's skip rule.

**Implementing files.** Attempts to break the design, each read in the tree:

- **Nested restore then outer restore: holds.** `noteObjectEntry` saves contributor references, so a nested put-back returns the same objects the outer record holds and `sitting.includes(contributor)` stays true. `adopt` keeps the outer run's earlier capture of a shared key; the captures are independent per key, so order does not matter.
- **Nested refusal caught by the reload: holds.** The nested record is dropped with its layers; the outer record still names the layer that was put back.
- **Engine maps written after a body's nested run: hold.** The manifest, datasource definitions, navigation contributions and kinds are recorded on the open outer run, so a refusal at the end takes them back. A stand-alone `registerApp` throws before those writes.
- **Cold boot against the sealed registry: holds.** Both askers read `bareNameHoldersAreSealed`; the boot-time `registerApp` callers run in `init` and `start`.
- **Partial failure: holds.** The refusal is thrown inside the `try`, so the catch restores, invalidates every fold and rethrows; `finally` reopens the outer record.
- **Tenant overlay, served layer: consistent both ways.** The pair is judged against the served parent and the unserved owner is skipped; ablation E and its control pin each side.
- **Body judged:** `judged` is the door's re-keyed output, the same body a single save asks about.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):

- N1. No registry-level pin for the nested path alone (caught nested refusal, then an outer refusal; a key the outer run wrote first). The reload cases reach it only indirectly.
- N2. The run's end is one door call per layer over every registered object; a reload of a large artifact pays that on each announce.
- N3. A follow amount contributed by an `extend` layer is judged by neither asker (the door's `partial` rule, unchanged from `main`); a card, not this PR.
- N4. A package skipped inside a reload can leave another package's pair incomplete, and the log then names the pair, not the skipped package.

No must-fix. The verdict is for the as-built reading of the open question; a ruling for the alternative moves the head and owes a fresh review. S1 and S2 owe a delta review by this reviewer.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e63ab141c1999ca3da4cd84a30259875d6128081`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.record-currency-follow-pair-refused-on-install-and-reload.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts, packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-artifact-refusal-restores.test.ts (the delta `e0d92b7b98..e63ab141c1`, two commits, no merge of `main`; the files the delta leaves untouched stand as reviewed in record 6839446638). Cited code, read and not reviewed: `resolveOwnerLayer` and `resolveObject` in packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts. The `.changeset` file and `content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx` are the lane seat's ACCEPT.

Delta review of record 6839446638 (PASS on `e0d92b7b98`, S1 and S2 should-fix). Ruling of record: card comment 6840575885, the maintainer's letter A, verbatim 「同意收窄,按 A 当场拒绝」.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged by the delta. Right.** `followRefusalAsServed` is reached only once a run is already refused. It returns the same refusal or one with the same class, object, field, code and status, so no install, upgrade or reload that was admitted is now refused, and none that was refused is now admitted.
- **Refusal text: one sentence added in one case. Right.** Where only the environment's own same-named object, served over a package's, earns the refusal, the message ends with a sentence naming that object. The class is still `RecordCurrencyFollowRefusedError`, so the reload's catch in `plugin.ts` still recognises it.
- **Public surface: none added.** `recordCurrencyFollowRefusalOverEnvironmentObjects` is exported from its module only; `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` does not re-export that module. `recordCurrencyFollowRefusalOf` stays private; its return type narrows and it gains an optional `lookup`.
- **One-end class: now declared. Right.** The entry's `surface`, `replacement` and `reason` say that a package holding one end is refused over the other end another package or the environment holds, also when its own objects did not change, and that the correction is the holder's.

### ② Semver level

- Unchanged and still right: `@objectstack/objectql` minor, `@objectstack/spec` patch, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, the ADR-0087 marker and entry id.
- The entry's new statements agree with the code: the one-end refusal (the door reads the other end from the registry), and the served-object case with no remedy promised, as ruling 6840575885 item 2 requires.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question of report 6839270777: closed** by ruling 6840575885 (letter A). Report 6841557774 carries `open_questions: []`.
- **Narrowing queued only on the maintainer's word: met** by the same ruling, item 1, once this record stands and the checks are green.
- **`security_findings: withheld` in report 6841557774.** One item is with the seat. No public text read for this review (the delta diff, both commit messages, the PR body, the changeset, the entry, report 6841557774) names how that state arises; each says only that the environment's own object of the same name is served over the package's and that the product has no remedy today.
- **Stale header in `registry-question.ts`:** now carried by #32934.
- **Check-runs on this head**, read at 2026-11-13T02:00Z: 16 succeeded, none failed. Still running: Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, both Lint · scoped jobs, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, and Type Check · consumer gates, debt ledger, source gates and workspace. Test UI and Type Check UI had not reported. This record does not stand in for any of them.

### ④ Design judgment

- **S1: closed.** The entry names the class and puts the correction on the holder of the declaration the refusal names. Two pins hold it in both directions, each followed by the correction that clears it: an unchanged parent re-registered over another package's child, and an unchanged child under another package's `record` roll-up.
- **S2: closed.** The entry and the changeset state the served-object case and say the product has no remedy for it today; neither promises one. The message sentence is built in one place and pinned to end the refusal; the control pins that a pair the package's own parent does not hold either is refused in the door's words alone. "No in-product remedy" rests on the dev's measurement outside the diff, as the PR body says; the diff does not prove it and does not claim to.
- **`followRefusalAsServed` against the code it cites: holds.**
  - It asks the same door once more with each tenant-authored overlay over an owner read through `resolveOwnerLayer` (the owner with its extenders folded), and adds the sentence only where that clears the refusal. The sentence's claim "read against the package's own definition this pair is not refused" is therefore checked, not assumed.
  - A refusal the package's own definitions also earn is returned unchanged (the control).
  - A refused layer that is itself the environment's object stays refused on the second reading, because the door reads the incoming body's own fields, so the sentence is not added there.
  - Only a refused run pays for the second question.
- **Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):**
  - N5. The fact sits at the tail of a message that is already about 300 characters. A door that answers through the 500-character client bound (`truncateClientMessage`) would cut it. Install-local builds its 422 body itself, so by reading it arrives whole there; no pin asserts the sentence in the install report.
  - N6. "The product has no remedy for it today" is now a string in code, the entry and the changeset. Whoever fixes the item with the seat must take all three out.
  - N7. The second reading folds every extender onto the owner, a disabled package's included, where the served fold withholds them.
  - N1 to N4 of record 6839446638 stand as accepted deviations.

No must-fix and no should-fix. This is the final round for this head.
